questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. On examination, the base is indurated and clean. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, firm, and non-tender. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents as a single, painless, indurated ulcer (chancre) with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Chancroid is painful, LGV causes tender nodes, and granuloma inguinale is a progressive, beefy-red ulcer.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops a butterfly-shaped erythematous rash over her cheeks and nose after sun exposure. She also reports joint pain and fatigue. ANA titre is 1:320 with anti-dsDNA positivity. The skin finding in this condition typically spares which area?
questions.exp: The malar (butterfly) rash of SLE characteristically spares the nasolabial folds, distinguishing it from rosacea and seborrheic dermatitis, both of which involve the nasolabial folds.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on multidrug therapy develops sudden facial palsy, tender thickening of the ulnar nerve, and new skin lesions appearing rapidly over 2 weeks. The correct management is:
opts: Stop MDT and start dapsone monotherapy
questions.exp: This is a Type 1 lepra reaction (reversal reaction) with nerve involvement. MDT must be continued without interruption while adding corticosteroids (prednisolone 40-60 mg/day) to reduce inflammation and prevent nerve damage.

questions.q: A 45-year-old immunocompetent man presents with itchy, scaly patches on the scalp with areas of hair loss. KOH mount shows large spores outside the hair shaft (ectothrix). The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes ectothrix tinea capitis with large-spore ectothrix pattern. Trichophyton tonsurans and T. violaceum cause endothrix pattern. Epidermophyton floccosum does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 60-year-old diabetic presents with rapidly spreading erythema, blistering, and necrosis over the scrotum and perineum with crepitus. The treatment of choice is:
opts: Urgent surgical debridement with IV antibiotics
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a rapidly fatal necrotising fasciitis of the genitoperineal region requiring emergency wide surgical debridement along with broad-spectrum IV antibiotics. Hyperbaric oxygen is adjunctive, not primary treatment.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops tense blisters on normal and erythematous skin. Nikolsky sign is negative. Biopsy shows subepidermal blister with eosinophilic infiltrate. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense blisters, negative Nikolsky sign, subepidermal bulla with eosinophils, and linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ on DIF. Pemphigus shows intraepidermal splits with net-like IgG. DH shows granular IgA at dermal papillae tips.

questions.q: A patient on long-term phenytoin therapy develops gum hypertrophy. He now presents with fixed, hyperpigmented patches on the trunk and extremities that recur at the same sites with each drug dose. This drug reaction is called:
questions.exp: Fixed drug eruption (FDE) recurs at the same anatomical site with each drug re-exposure, leaving residual hyperpigmentation. Common culprits include phenytoin, sulfonamides, and NSAIDs.

questions.q: A 50-year-old farmer presents with a warty, verrucous plaque with sinus tracts on the lower leg. Biopsy shows 'copper penny' bodies (Medlar bodies). The most common causative organism in India is:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is characterised by Medlar (sclerotic) bodies on histology. Fonsecaea pedrosoi is the most common causative agent worldwide and in India. Sporothrix causes sporotrichosis; Madurella causes eumycetoma.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with grouped, umbilicated, pearly papules on the face, neck, and trunk. CD4 count is 80 cells/µL. The condition is caused by:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum caused by a poxvirus (MCV) presents as umbilicated, pearly papules. In immunocompromised patients (low CD4), it becomes extensive and giant lesions can occur on the face.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, thickening of skin over fingers and forearms, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibodies are positive. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Diffuse cutaneous SSc is associated with anti-Scl-70 antibodies and involves skin proximal to elbows/knees. CREST syndrome (limited SSc) is associated with anti-centromere antibodies.

questions.q: A 22-year-old student presents with well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery scales over the elbows and knees for 2 years. Histopathology would show:
opts: Parakeratosis, elongated rete ridges, and Munro microabscesses
Lichenoid infiltrate at the dermo-epidermal junction
questions.exp: Psoriasis histology shows regular elongation of rete ridges, parakeratosis, absent or reduced granular layer, Munro microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum), and suprapapillary plate thinning.

questions.q: A child presents with 3 hypopigmented anaesthetic patches and one thickened nerve. Slit-skin smear is negative. According to WHO classification, this is:
questions.exp: WHO classifies leprosy as paucibacillary (PB) if skin smear is negative and there are up to 5 skin lesions and up to 1 nerve trunk involved. This patient has 3 patches and 1 nerve — PB classification.

questions.q: A 35-year-old sex worker presents with multiple painful genital ulcers with ragged, undermined edges and associated tender inguinal lymph nodes (bubo). Gram stain of bubo aspirate shows gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' pattern. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, presents with painful ulcers and tender inguinal buboes. Gram stain shows gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' or 'railway track' pattern (Ducrey's bacillus).

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a pigmented lesion on the sole that has grown over 6 months. Dermoscopy reveals irregular pigment network, blue-white veil, and atypical vascular patterns. The most appropriate next step is:
opts: Punch biopsy from the darkest area
questions.exp: Suspected melanoma requires excisional biopsy with narrow margins (1-2 mm) to allow accurate Breslow thickness measurement for staging, which guides further wide excision margins. Punch biopsy can miss the thickest area.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent papule with rolled borders and telangiectasias on the nose, present for 2 years with intermittent bleeding. Histopathology shows palisading nuclei at the periphery of tumour nests with retraction artefact. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (nodular type) presents as a pearly papule with rolled edges and telangiectasias. Histology shows palisading of nuclei at the periphery of basaloid nests with a characteristic peritumoral retraction artefact.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman on oral contraceptives develops a symmetrical brown discolouration over the cheeks, upper lip, and forehead that worsens in summer. Wood's lamp shows enhancement of pigmentation. Diagnosis and preferred treatment are:
opts: Melasma; triple combination cream (hydroquinone + tretinoin + steroid)
Nevus of Ota; Q-switched Nd:YAG laser
questions.exp: Melasma presents as symmetric facial hyperpigmentation enhanced by Wood's lamp (epidermal type). Triple combination cream (Kligman's formula: hydroquinone 4% + tretinoin 0.05% + fluocinolone 0.01%) is the gold standard treatment.

questions.q: A neonate develops blistering at birth. The mother has pemphigus vulgaris currently in remission. The most likely explanation for the neonatal blistering is:
opts: Passive transfer of maternal IgG anti-desmoglein antibodies across the placenta
questions.exp: Neonatal pemphigus occurs due to passive placental transfer of maternal IgG anti-desmoglein 1 and/or 3 antibodies. It is transient and resolves as maternal antibodies are cleared over weeks.

questions.q: A patient presents with a solitary, pigmented plaque on the palm since childhood, with irregular borders and multiple colours. Dermoscopy shows parallel ridge pattern. The most appropriate management is:
questions.exp: Parallel ridge pattern on acral dermoscopy (palms/soles) is a highly specific indicator of acral lentiginous melanoma. Urgent excision biopsy is required. Parallel furrow pattern indicates benign acral nevus.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with violaceous, oedematous periorbital discolouration (heliotrope rash) and erythematous papules over metacarpophalangeal joints (Gottron's papules). CK is markedly elevated. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis is characterised by heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules/sign, and proximal muscle weakness with elevated muscle enzymes. It is associated with underlying malignancy in adults over 40.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with a painless, slowly enlarging ulcer on the genitalia with beefy-red granulation tissue. Lesions bleed easily on contact. Biopsy shows 'Donovan bodies' (encapsulated bacteria within macrophages). Treatment of choice is:
opts: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 3 weeks
questions.exp: Granuloma inguinale (Donovanosis) caused by Klebsiella granulomatis shows Donovan bodies on tissue smear. Azithromycin 1 g weekly (or 500 mg daily) for minimum 3 weeks is the preferred treatment per WHO/CDC guidelines.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child has multiple moth-eaten alopecia patches on the scalp with broken hairs ('black dot' appearance). KOH shows chains of spores inside the hair shaft. Wood's lamp is negative. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Trichophyton tonsurans causes endothrix tinea capitis (black dot pattern) with spores filling the inside of the hair. It does not fluoresce under Wood's lamp. Microsporum species fluoresce green and cause ectothrix pattern.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents to a dermatology clinic for removal of a 4-mm non-melanoma skin cancer on the nose. The technique offering the highest cure rate with maximal tissue conservation is:
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery offers the highest cure rates (98-99% for primary BCC) with maximal normal tissue conservation by examining 100% of surgical margins intraoperatively. It is especially indicated for high-risk sites like the nose.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops a diffuse, fiery red, tender erythema over the face, trunk, and extremities 2 weeks after starting lamotrigine. She has fever, lymphadenopathy, and liver function test derangement. The diagnosis is:
opts: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
questions.exp: DRESS presents 2-6 weeks after drug initiation with diffuse erythema, fever, lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia, and multi-organ involvement. Anticonvulsants like lamotrigine, carbamazepine, and phenytoin are common triggers.

questions.q: A 45-year-old presents with multiple painful, red, nodular swellings on the shins, associated with fever and malaise. She is known to have sarcoidosis. Histology of the lesion shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is the most common panniculitis, presenting as tender red nodules on shins. It is a septal panniculitis without vasculitis. Common triggers include sarcoidosis, streptococcal infections, TB, and drugs (OCP, sulfonamides).

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with vesicles and bullae on extensor surfaces and buttocks associated with coeliac disease. Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin shows granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae tips. Diagnosis and treatment are:
opts: Dermatitis herpetiformis; dapsone and gluten-free diet
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis is associated with coeliac disease. Granular IgA at dermal papillae tips on DIF is pathognomonic. Treatment is dapsone for quick symptom relief plus strict gluten-free diet for long-term remission.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with erythematous, scaly plaques affecting the scalp, face, and upper trunk. Biopsy shows follicular plugging, interface dermatitis, and deep perivascular infiltrate with periadnexal inflammation. Scarring alopecia is present. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE) causes scarring skin lesions with follicular plugging. Histology reveals interface dermatitis, follicular plugging, and periadnexal infiltrate. DLE rarely progresses to systemic lupus.

questions.q: A patient being treated with dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops sudden haemolytic anaemia and methaemoglobinaemia. Which enzyme deficiency makes patients most susceptible to dapsone toxicity?
questions.exp: G6PD deficiency predisposes to dapsone-induced haemolytic anaemia because the pentose phosphate pathway (dependent on G6PD) is needed to regenerate NADPH, which protects red cells from oxidative damage by dapsone metabolites.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with itchy, flesh-coloured, flat-topped polygonal papules on the flexor aspects of wrists and ankles. Oral mucosa shows lacy white streaks (Wickham's striae). Histopathology is most likely to show:
opts: Sawtooth rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ, civatte bodies
questions.exp: Lichen planus histology shows hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, sawtooth rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate hugging the DEJ, and Civatte (colloid/cytoid) bodies (necrotic basal keratinocytes). Wickham's striae correspond to hypergranulosis.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-coloured crusted lesions around the nose and mouth that spread rapidly. Gram stain of crust shows gram-positive cocci in chains. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo is caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes, presenting with honey-coloured crusts. Topical mupirocin is first-line for localised disease; oral flucloxacillin or amoxicillin-clavulanate for widespread disease.

questions.q: A 40-year-old presents with a 2-cm hypopigmented patch on the cheek with loss of sensation to pinprick. Single skin smear is negative. There are no thickened peripheral nerves. Biopsy shows non-specific lymphocytic infiltrate around superficial nerve twigs with no granuloma. This is classified as:
questions.exp: Indeterminate leprosy is the earliest and most uncertain form with a single hypopigmented patch, minimal sensory loss, negative smear, and non-specific histology without granuloma formation. It may resolve spontaneously or progress to a definite type.

questions.q: A 50-year-old HIV-positive man presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the T5 dermatome, not crossing the midline. He also has new neurological deficits. The causative virus is:
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (shingles) is caused by reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus (VZV) from dorsal root ganglia. In immunocompromised patients, it can disseminate or cause neurological complications. Dermatomal distribution is characteristic.
